## Purpose

**Can we get Cinnamon Teal, or other waterfowl, data specifically for the
Klamath region, in both California and Oregon?**

This document assesses each source we are given and records whether it can
answer that question for each state, and at what spatial grain. Sources are
added one at a time. The summary table below is the running answer, and each
report gets its own section after it.

# Report 1: CDFW California Waterfowl Breeding Population Survey

**Source:** [Waterfowl Breeding Population - California - 1992-2022](https://data.ca.gov/@california-department-of-fish-and-wildlife/waterfowl-breeding-population-california-1992-2022),
California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW), Waterfowl Program (data
package `dmp000455`, saved in `data-raw/waterfowl/dmp000455_data`). CDFW
asks that uses acknowledge "CA Department of Fish and Wildlife/Waterfowl
Program", funded by Pittman-Robertson and State Duck Stamp funds, and that
users contact the data manager to discuss appropriate analyses.

**Also used:** Brady, C., and M. Weaver. 2026. *2026 California Waterfowl
Breeding Population Survey Report*. CDFW Waterfowl Unit. PDF in
`data-raw/waterfowl/reports/`. **This report was not included in the direct
download from the data.ca.gov waterfowl dataset** (`dmp000455`, which ends with
the 2022 report); it was provided separately.

**Temporal Coverage:** Annual, 1992-2026 (not flown in 2020 or 2021). Flown the
second week of May in northeastern California (6-7 May in 2026). The annual
reports in the download cover 2003-2022; the 2026 report extends the by-stratum
series through 2026 (2023-2025 appear only there).

**Spatial Grain:** Stratum for counts (9 strata statewide); segment for the
mallard index only. Flight legs and waypoints are mapped.

**Klamath coverage:** Partial. The Klamath is inside the Northeastern California
stratum, and 16 flight legs and 24 waypoints are in the basin. California side
only; no Oregon refuges.

**Species:** 19 species on the survey sheet (2003-2015); mallard, gadwall,
Cinnamon Teal and Canada goose by stratum (2016-2026).

**Findings:** No Klamath-specific Cinnamon Teal counts (stratum only). Mallards
have a segment-level index on all eight Klamath segments. Details below.

## What is in the folder

```{r inventory}
inventory <- read_csv(
  here("data-raw", "waterfowl", "dmp000455_data_inventory.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

inventory |>
  count(category, name = "files", sort = TRUE) |>
  kable()
```

## How the survey works

From the CDFW metadata worksheet in the folder:

-   Flown by fixed-wing aircraft and helicopter, two observers in each.
-   Conducted about the third week of April in the Central Valley and the
    second week of May in northeastern California.
-   California is divided into nine **strata**, each sampled by transects
    made of segments. Species, sex, and breeding status are recorded.
-   The survey has run since 1955; the current design dates from 1992. It
    was not flown in 2020 or 2021.
-   Counts are expressed as **total indicated birds** (TIB): a
    breeding-pair index that weights lone drakes, pairs, flocked drakes,
    and groups differently by species. Population estimates correct TIB for
    detectability using a visibility correction factor (VCF) and expand it
    by stratum area.
-   Spatial detail: "Data collected on transect within Stratum. For some
    years, lat-long associated with each observation."

## Cinnamon Teal: statewide

`cinnamon_teal_population` holds the statewide estimates compiled for this
package.

```{r teal-statewide}
cinnamon_teal_population |>
  mutate(run = cumsum(c(TRUE, diff(year) > 1))) |>   # break the line across survey gaps
  ggplot(aes(year, pop_est)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = ci_low, ymax = ci_high, group = run), alpha = 0.2, fill = "#2a78d6", na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_line(aes(group = run), color = "#2a78d6") +
  geom_point(color = "#2a78d6") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(
    title = "Statewide Cinnamon Teal breeding population estimate",
    subtitle = "As compiled in cinnamon_teal_population; ribbon is the 95% interval where reported",
    x = NULL, y = "Estimated birds"
  )
```

## Cinnamon Teal: by stratum

The annual reports break the estimate down by stratum. Appendix IV of the 2026
report has Cinnamon Teal for all nine strata, 1992 to 2026. It was not in the
direct download, which ends with the 2022 report, so 2023-2026 come only from
the 2026 report.

```{r teal-strata}
reports_dir <- here("data-raw", "waterfowl", "reports")

# Cinnamon Teal block of Appendix IV from a report PDF: year rows only
read_teal_appendix <- function(pdf) {
  pages <- pdf_text(pdf)
  page <- which(str_detect(pages, "Appendix IV\\. Continued") & str_detect(pages, "Cinnamon Teal"))
  stopifnot(length(page) == 1)

  lines <- strsplit(pages[page], "\n")[[1]]
  header <- str_split(trimws(grep("^\\s*Year\\s+SV", lines, value = TRUE)), "\\s+")[[1]]
  rows <- str_split(trimws(grep("^\\s*(19|20)\\d{2}\\s+\\d", lines, value = TRUE)), "\\s+")

  out <- map(rows, \(x) set_names(as.numeric(gsub(",", "", x)), header)) |>
    map(\(x) as_tibble(as.list(x))) |>
    list_rbind() |>
    rename(year = Year) |>
    mutate(ne_share = NE / TOTAL)

  # The strata should add up to the statewide total in every year.
  stopifnot(all(abs(rowSums(out[setdiff(header, c("Year", "TOTAL"))]) - out$TOTAL) <= 2))
  out
}

teal_strata <- read_teal_appendix(file.path(reports_dir, "2026 CA BPS Report Final.pdf"))
teal_strata_2022 <- read_teal_appendix(file.path(survey_dir, "2022 CA BPS Report Final.pdf"))

# Guards the numbers quoted in the text and Summary table.
stopifnot(
  range(teal_strata$year) == c(1992, 2026),
  teal_strata$NE[teal_strata$year == 2026] == 28077,
  teal_strata$TOTAL[teal_strata$year == 2026] == 39745
)
```

```{r teal-strata-plot}
teal_strata |>
  transmute(year, `Northeastern California` = NE, Statewide = TOTAL) |>
  pivot_longer(-year, names_to = "series", values_to = "estimate") |>
  mutate(run = cumsum(c(TRUE, diff(year) > 1)), .by = series) |>
  ggplot(aes(year, estimate, color = series, group = interaction(series, run))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Statewide = "grey40", `Northeastern California` = "#eb6834"), name = NULL) +
  labs(
    title = "Cinnamon Teal: Northeastern California stratum vs statewide",
    subtitle = "The Klamath is one part of the Northeastern stratum",
    x = NULL, y = "Estimated birds"
  )
```

The Northeastern stratum accounts for a median
`r scales::percent(median(teal_strata$ne_share), accuracy = 1)` of the
statewide estimate (range
`r scales::percent(min(teal_strata$ne_share), accuracy = 1)` to
`r scales::percent(max(teal_strata$ne_share), accuracy = 1)`) across
`r nrow(teal_strata)` survey years.

**2026 report vs the 2022 report.** The two appendices overlap for 1992-2022.

```{r teal-2022-check}
overlap <- inner_join(
  teal_strata_2022 |> select(year, NE_2022 = NE, TOTAL_2022 = TOTAL),
  teal_strata |> select(year, NE_2026 = NE, TOTAL_2026 = TOTAL),
  by = "year"
)

overlap |>
  filter(NE_2022 != NE_2026 | TOTAL_2022 != TOTAL_2026) |>
  mutate(year = as.character(year)) |>
  kable(
    format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
    col.names = c("Year", "NE (2022 report)", "Total (2022 report)", "NE (2026 report)", "Total (2026 report)"),
    caption = "Years where the two reports differ"
  )

# Only the 2022 estimate was revised; the new years are 2023-2026.
stopifnot(
  all(overlap$year[overlap$NE_2022 != overlap$NE_2026] == 2022),
  setequal(setdiff(teal_strata$year, teal_strata_2022$year), 2023:2026)
)
```

`r sum(overlap$NE_2022 == overlap$NE_2026)` of `r nrow(overlap)` overlapping
years are identical for the Northeastern stratum. The 2026 report revises 2022
slightly and adds 2023-2026.

How the packaged object compares to the report appendix:

```{r teal-object-check}
object_check <- cinnamon_teal_population |>
  inner_join(teal_strata |> select(year, TOTAL), by = "year") |>
  mutate(diff = pop_est - TOTAL)

object_check |>
  filter(abs(diff) > 1) |>
  select(year, packaged = pop_est, appendix = TOTAL, diff) |>
  kable(digits = 0, caption = "Years where cinnamon_teal_population differs from Appendix IV")
```

`r sum(abs(object_check$diff) <= 1)` of `r nrow(object_check)` overlapping years
match exactly. The appendix also covers
`r length(setdiff(teal_strata$year, cinnamon_teal_population$year))` survey years
that the packaged object lacks
(`r paste(range(setdiff(teal_strata$year, cinnamon_teal_population$year)), collapse = "-")`).

## Where the survey samples the Klamath

The survey's flight legs and waypoints that fall in the Klamath Basin (the 12
HUC8 subbasins of `rivermile::klamath_hucs`), read from the KML and CSV files in
the CDFW folder. These are built here for exploration and are not saved as
package data.

```{r klamath-geometry}
gis_dir <- file.path(
  survey_dir,
  "California Breeding Waterfowl Survey GIS info for Air Services",
  "California Breeding Waterfowl Survey GIS info for Air Services"
)

# boundaries ---------------------------------------------------------------

basin <- rivermile::klamath_hucs |>
  st_union() |>
  st_transform(5070)

# Same refuge names and 0.5-mile buffer used for `area` in this package's other datasets.
refuges_buffered <- rivermile::klamath_refuges |>
  mutate(
    area = case_when(
      str_detect(orgname, "bear valley")   ~ "Bear Valley",
      str_detect(orgname, "clear lake")    ~ "Clear Lake",
      str_detect(orgname, "klamath marsh") ~ "Klamath Marsh",
      str_detect(orgname, "lower klamath") ~ "Lower Klamath - Sheepy",
      str_detect(orgname, "tule lake")     ~ "Tule Lake",
      str_detect(orgname, "upper klamath") ~ "Upper Klamath Lake"
    )
  ) |>
  select(area) |>
  st_buffer(units::set_units(0.5, "mi")) |>
  st_transform(5070)

# Refuge (buffered) that a feature touches, or NA. A feature in the overlap of
# two buffers lists both.
refuge_of <- function(x) {
  hit <- st_intersects(st_transform(x, 5070), refuges_buffered)
  vapply(
    hit,
    \(i) if (length(i)) paste(refuges_buffered$area[i], collapse = " + ") else NA_character_,
    character(1)
  )
}

# transects ----------------------------------------------------------------
#
# The KML is a Google Earth export of the survey shapefile. Each Placemark is a
# leg between two waypoints; its Comment ends with the waypoint pair, e.g.
# "(254-255)". sf does not expose the KML's ExtendedData, so parse the XML.

kml <- read_xml(file.path(gis_dir, "California Breeding Waterfowl Survey All Segments.kml"))
xml_ns_strip(kml)

parse_leg <- function(placemark) {
  fields <- xml_find_all(placemark, ".//SimpleData")
  coords <- trimws(xml_text(xml_find_first(placemark, ".//LineString/coordinates")))
  xy <- do.call(rbind, lapply(strsplit(strsplit(coords, "\\s+")[[1]], ","), as.numeric))
  list(
    attrs = as_tibble(as.list(setNames(xml_text(fields), xml_attr(fields, "name")))),
    geom  = st_linestring(xy[, 1:2, drop = FALSE])
  )
}

legs_raw <- lapply(xml_find_all(kml, "//Placemark"), parse_leg)

legs_all <- st_sf(
  bind_rows(lapply(legs_raw, `[[`, "attrs")),
  geometry = st_sfc(lapply(legs_raw, `[[`, "geom"), crs = 4326)
)

# Keep legs that touch the basin. Source `Segment` codes are not unique and
# disagree with Str/Trn/Seg for some legs (e.g. code 090719 on segment 18), so
# key on the segment number (Seg), which matches the waypoint file and maps.
#
# The source `Length_mi` is not used. For all 106 legs statewide the geodesic
# length of the line is cos(latitude) times Length_mi (about 0.75 at the
# Klamath), as if a degree of longitude were as long as a degree of latitude.
# `length_km` below is computed from the geometry instead.
touches_basin <- lengths(st_intersects(st_transform(legs_all, 5070), basin)) > 0

legs <- legs_all[touches_basin, ]

km_in_basin <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(legs)), \(i) {
  piece <- suppressWarnings(st_intersection(st_transform(st_geometry(legs)[i], 5070), basin))
  if (length(piece) == 0) 0 else sum(as.numeric(st_length(piece))) / 1000
}, numeric(1))

wp_pair <- str_match(legs$Comment, "\\((\\d+)-(\\d+)\\)\\s*$")

klamath_legs <- legs |>
  transmute(
    stratum       = "Northeastern California",
    transect      = as.integer(Trn),
    segment       = as.integer(Seg),
    from_waypoint = as.integer(wp_pair[, 2]),
    to_waypoint   = as.integer(wp_pair[, 3]),
    description   = str_squish(str_remove(Comment, "\\(\\d+-\\d+\\)\\s*$")),
    vcf_old       = VCF == "Yes",
    vcf_2019      = New_VCF__1 == "Yes",
    length_km     = round(as.numeric(st_length(geometry)) / 1000, 2),
    km_in_basin   = round(km_in_basin, 2),
    area          = refuge_of(geometry)
  ) |>
  arrange(segment, from_waypoint)

stopifnot(
  all(legs$Str == "9"),                       # stratum 9 = Northeastern California
  !anyNA(klamath_legs$from_waypoint)
)

# waypoints ----------------------------------------------------------------

waypoints_all <- read_csv(
  file.path(gis_dir, "California Breeding Waterfowl Survey Waypoints For Plane.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

waypoints_sf <- st_as_sf(waypoints_all, coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)
in_basin <- lengths(st_intersects(st_transform(waypoints_sf, 5070), basin)) > 0

klamath_waypoints <- waypoints_sf[in_basin, ] |>
  transmute(
    stratum  = Strata,
    segment  = as.integer(Segment),
    waypoint = as.integer(Waypoint),
    comment  = str_squish(Comment),
    vcf_old  = `Old VCF` == "Yes",
    vcf_2019 = `New VCF (2019)` == "Yes",
    area     = refuge_of(geometry)
  ) |>
  arrange(waypoint)

stopifnot(all(klamath_waypoints$stratum == "Northeastern California"))

# Each leg should run between the two waypoints named in its comment.
wp_xy <- st_transform(waypoints_sf, 5070)
leg_end_gap_km <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(klamath_legs)), \(i) {
  leg <- st_transform(klamath_legs[i, ], 5070)
  ends <- st_cast(st_geometry(leg), "POINT")[c(1, length(st_cast(st_geometry(leg), "POINT")))]
  w <- wp_xy[match(c(leg$from_waypoint, leg$to_waypoint), waypoints_all$Waypoint), ]
  d <- st_distance(ends, st_geometry(w))
  min(sum(c(d[1, 1], d[2, 2])), sum(c(d[1, 2], d[2, 1]))) / 2 / 1000
}, numeric(1))
stopifnot(max(leg_end_gap_km) < 1)
```

```{r klamath-map}
hucs <- st_transform(rivermile::klamath_hucs, 4326)
refuges <- rivermile::klamath_refuges

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = hucs, fill = "grey95", color = "grey75", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = refuges, fill = "#bcd7ee", color = "#2a78d6", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = klamath_legs, aes(color = vcf_old), linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_sf(data = klamath_waypoints, size = 1.3, color = "grey20") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 42, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey45") +
  annotate("text", x = -123.9, y = 42.04, label = "California / Oregon line (42 N)",
           hjust = 0, size = 3, color = "grey35") +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(`FALSE` = "#eb6834", `TRUE` = "#1baf7a"),
    labels = c(`FALSE` = "no", `TRUE` = "yes"),
    name = "Old-design VCF segment"
  ) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-124, -120.4), ylim = c(41.2, 42.4)) +
  labs(
    title = "CDFW breeding survey legs and waypoints in the Klamath Basin",
    subtitle = "Blue = refuges. The survey flies California only.",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  )
```

```{r klamath-design-facts}
n_legs <- nrow(klamath_legs)
n_waypoints <- nrow(klamath_waypoints)
km_in_basin <- sum(klamath_legs$km_in_basin)

# Guards the static text in the Summary table.
stopifnot(n_legs == 16, n_waypoints == 24)

# The 2026 report says transect-segment 7-20 was not flown; check it is ours.
unflown_2026 <- klamath_legs |> filter(transect == 7, segment == 20)
stopifnot(nrow(unflown_2026) == 2)
```

`r n_legs` legs (`r round(km_in_basin)` km inside the basin) and `r n_waypoints`
waypoints, all in the Northeastern California stratum. A **leg** runs between
two waypoints; a **segment** groups one or more legs.

**2026 survey.** The 2026 report says transect-segment 7-20 in northeastern
California was not flown because of high winds, leaving the survey 95% complete
in that region. Segment 20 is one of the Klamath segments here
(`r nrow(unflown_2026)` legs: `r paste(unflown_2026$description, collapse = "; ")`).

## Geographic coverage: California only

```{r coverage}
# The California-Oregon line is the 42nd parallel.
south_of_42 <- st_as_sfc(st_bbox(c(xmin = -125, ymin = 39, xmax = -118, ymax = 42), crs = 4326))
area_m2 <- \(x) as.numeric(st_area(st_transform(x, 5070)))

coverage <- refuges |>
  mutate(
    area = case_when(
      str_detect(orgname, "bear valley")   ~ "Bear Valley",
      str_detect(orgname, "clear lake")    ~ "Clear Lake",
      str_detect(orgname, "klamath marsh") ~ "Klamath Marsh",
      str_detect(orgname, "lower klamath") ~ "Lower Klamath - Sheepy",
      str_detect(orgname, "tule lake")     ~ "Tule Lake",
      str_detect(orgname, "upper klamath") ~ "Upper Klamath Lake"
    ),
    pct_in_california = map_dbl(seq_len(n()), \(i) {
      s <- suppressWarnings(st_intersection(st_geometry(refuges)[i], south_of_42))
      if (length(s) == 0) 0 else 100 * sum(area_m2(s)) / area_m2(st_geometry(refuges)[i])
    })
  ) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  left_join(
    klamath_legs |> st_drop_geometry() |> filter(!is.na(area)) |> count(area, name = "legs_crossing"),
    by = "area"
  ) |>
  left_join(
    klamath_waypoints |> st_drop_geometry() |> filter(!is.na(area)) |> count(area, name = "waypoints_inside"),
    by = "area"
  ) |>
  mutate(across(c(legs_crossing, waypoints_inside), \(x) replace_na(x, 0L))) |>
  select(refuge = area, pct_in_california, legs_crossing, waypoints_inside)

kable(coverage, digits = 0,
      caption = "Refuge coverage by the survey (legs and waypoints use a 0.5-mile refuge buffer)")
```

The northernmost survey waypoint is at
`r round(max(waypoints_all$Latitude), 3)` degrees north, so
`r sum(waypoints_all$Latitude > 42)` of `r nrow(waypoints_all)` waypoints are in
Oregon. Upper Klamath and Klamath Marsh are entirely in Oregon and are not
sampled; Bear Valley is mostly in Oregon.

## Segment-level counts: mallards only

The one segment-level count table in the folder is Appendix V of the 2019
report: a five-year average (2014-2018, fixed-wing) of mallard TIB for each of
the 21 Northeastern segments.

```{r mallard-segments}
lines_2019 <- pdf_text(file.path(survey_dir, "BPS annual report 2019  Final.pdf")) |>
  paste(collapse = "\n") |>
  str_split("\n") |>
  pluck(1)

start <- grep("Appendix V\\. Five-year", lines_2019)
block <- str_match(lines_2019[start:(start + 40)], "^\\s*(\\d{1,2})\\s+([0-9.]+)\\s*(.*)$")

mallard_segments <- block[!is.na(block[, 1]) & as.integer(block[, 2]) <= 21, 2:4, drop = FALSE] |>
  as_tibble(.name_repair = "minimal") |>
  set_names(c("segment", "mallard_tib", "comment")) |>
  mutate(segment = as.integer(segment), mallard_tib = as.numeric(mallard_tib), comment = trimws(comment)) |>
  distinct(segment, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(klamath = segment %in% 14:21, rank = rank(-mallard_tib, ties.method = "min"))

# The report's own text quotes the five-year means for segments 1, 3, 6 and 8.
stopifnot(
  nrow(mallard_segments) == 21,
  identical(mallard_segments$mallard_tib[mallard_segments$segment %in% c(1, 3, 6, 8)], c(29, 21.2, 98.6, 134.4)),
  all(mallard_segments$mallard_tib[mallard_segments$klamath] > 0)   # guards the Summary text
)
```

```{r mallard-segments-plot}
ggplot(mallard_segments, aes(factor(segment), mallard_tib, fill = klamath)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey70", `TRUE` = "#2a78d6"),
                    labels = c(`FALSE` = "other Northeastern segments", `TRUE` = "Klamath segments (14-21)"),
                    name = NULL) +
  labs(
    title = "Mallard total indicated birds by Northeastern survey segment",
    subtitle = "Five-year average, 2014-2018 (2019 report, Appendix V)",
    x = "Segment", y = "Mallard TIB"
  )
```

```{r mallard-segments-table}
klamath_legs |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  summarise(where = str_trunc(paste(unique(description), collapse = "; "), 80), .by = segment) |>
  left_join(mallard_segments |> select(segment, mallard_tib, rank), by = "segment") |>
  arrange(segment) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Segment", "Where (leg descriptions)", "Mallard TIB", "Rank of 21"),
        caption = "Klamath segments")
```

Mallards were counted on all eight Klamath segments. Together they hold
`r scales::percent(sum(mallard_segments$mallard_tib[mallard_segments$klamath]) / sum(mallard_segments$mallard_tib), accuracy = 1)`
of the stratum's mallard TIB while being 8 of 21 segments (mean
`r round(mean(mallard_segments$mallard_tib[mallard_segments$klamath]), 1)` vs
`r round(mean(mallard_segments$mallard_tib[!mallard_segments$klamath]), 1)` for the
other segments). These are whole-segment indices, not densities, and they cover
mallards only.

## Species in the Northeastern stratum

The 2003-2015 reports' "Summary B" tables give every survey-sheet species for
each stratum. The Northeastern California block:

```{r species}
report_files <- c(
  "2003" = "ca-pop2003.doc", "2004" = "ca-pop2004.doc", "2005" = "ca-pop2005.doc",
  "2006" = "ca-pop2006.doc", "2007" = "ca-pop2007.doc", "2008" = "ca-pop2008.doc",
  "2009" = "ca-pop_2009.doc", "2010" = "ca-po2010.doc", "2011" = "2011 ca_bpop_rep1.docx",
  "2012" = "2012 ca_bpop_rep1.txt", "2013" = "2013 ca_bpop_rep1.docx",
  "2014" = "2014 ca_bpop_rep1.docx", "2015" = "2015 ca_bpop_rep1.docx"
)

species_row <- "^\\s*(\\d{4})\\s+([A-Za-z][A-Za-z .'-]*?)\\s+(\\d+)\\s+(\\d+)\\s+(\\d+)\\s+\\((\\d+),\\s*([0-9?]+)\\)"

ne_species <- imap(report_files, \(file, year) {
  text <- read_report(file.path(survey_dir, file))
  header <- grep("Northeastern Cal.*\\(EF", text)[1]
  first_stratum <- str_match(text[header], "^\\s*([A-Za-z/ ]+?)\\s*\\(EF")[, 2]
  stopifnot(str_detect(first_stratum, "Northeastern"))   # NE is the first stratum on its header

  rows <- str_match(text[(header + 1):min(length(text), header + 45)], species_row)
  rows <- rows[!is.na(rows[, 1]) & !duplicated(rows[, 2]), , drop = FALSE]
  stopifnot(nrow(rows) >= 19)

  tibble(year = as.integer(year), aou = rows[1:19, 2], species = trimws(rows[1:19, 3]),
         tib = as.numeric(rows[1:19, 4]), estimate = as.numeric(rows[1:19, 5]))
}) |>
  list_rbind()

# Species names vary between reports; use the 2012 spelling for each AOU code.
ne_species <- ne_species |>
  select(-species) |>
  left_join(ne_species |> filter(year == 2012) |> select(aou, species), by = "aou")

species_summary <- ne_species |>
  summarise(
    years_detected = sum(estimate > 0),
    median_estimate = median(estimate[estimate > 0]),
    max_estimate = max(estimate),
    .by = species
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(years_detected), desc(median_estimate))

# Guards the Summary text.
stopifnot(sum(species_summary$years_detected > 0) == 18, n_distinct(ne_species$year) == 13)

species_summary |>
  mutate(across(c(median_estimate, max_estimate), \(x) round(x))) |>
  kable(
    col.names = c("Species", "Years detected (of 13)", "Median estimate when present", "Maximum estimate"),
    format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
    caption = "Northeastern California stratum, 2003-2015"
  )
```

The two checks below confirm the parse: Cinnamon Teal for the stratum should
match Appendix IV in every overlapping year.

```{r species-check}
check <- ne_species |>
  filter(species == "Cinnamon Teal") |>
  inner_join(teal_strata |> select(year, appendix = NE), by = "year")

tibble(
  years_compared = nrow(check),
  exact_matches = sum(abs(check$estimate - check$appendix) <= 1)
) |>
  kable()
```

For 2016-2022 only mallard, gadwall, Cinnamon Teal and Canada goose are broken
out by stratum (Appendix IV). The stratum is much larger than the Klamath, so
none of this isolates the Klamath.

## Conclusion for Report 1

**We cannot pull Cinnamon Teal data specific to the Klamath region of
California from this dataset.**

-   **Counts are by stratum.** Cinnamon Teal is estimated for the Northeastern
    California stratum, which also covers places such as Alturas and
    Susanville. The Klamath cannot be separated from it.
-   **Segment-level counts are mallard-only.** Mallards were counted on all
    eight Klamath segments (five-year average, 2014-2018). There is nothing
    equivalent for Cinnamon Teal or other species, and nothing at the waypoint
    level.
-   **California only.** The Oregon side of the basin is not surveyed. In
    California, flight lines cross only Tule Lake and Lower Klamath directly.
-   **Finer records are not in the folder.** The metadata says observations
    have locations for some years, but those records were not provided.

On "waterfowl" generally: we **can** say that waterfowl occur regionally (18 of
19 survey-sheet species in the Northeastern stratum, 2003-2015) and that
mallards were counted on every Klamath segment. We cannot say which other
species were counted in the Klamath or how many.

**What we can provide from this report:** where the survey samples the basin,
the Northeastern stratum series by species, and the mallard segment-level index.

**Next step:** ask CDFW's Waterfowl Program (contact listed in the dataset
metadata) for Cinnamon Teal and other species' counts by segment and year for
segments 14-21, plus any observation-level records with locations.

# Report 2: Fleskes and Yee (2007), spring waterfowl in southern Oregon and northeastern California

**Source:** Fleskes, J. P., and J. L. Yee. 2007. [Waterfowl distribution and
abundance during spring migration in southern Oregon and northeastern
California](https://scholarsarchive.byu.edu/wnan/vol67/iss3/10). *Western North
American Naturalist* 67(3):409-428. U.S. Geological Survey, Western Ecological
Research Center. Table 4 (p. 422) is the table used here. PDF in
`data-raw/waterfowl/reports/`.

**Temporal Coverage:** Two springs, 5 January-3 May 2002 and 2003 (six aerial
surveys each). Table 4 is the 2002-2003 average.

**Spatial Grain:** Subregion. The study area, called SONEC (southern Oregon and
northeastern California; 70,491 km^2^), has 11 subregions. Seven core
subregions plus the Madeline Plains were surveyed; Table 4 reports 7 columns.
Fig. 2 of the paper shows each subregion by survey date, as bar charts without
values.

**Klamath coverage:** Yes, through two subregions. *Lower Klamath* includes
Lower Klamath, Tule Lake and Clear Lake NWRs, Butte Valley WA and the Klamath
River State Game Management Area. *Upper Klamath* includes Upper Klamath and
Klamath Marsh NWRs, Upper Klamath and Agency Lakes, and Sycan Marsh. The map
(Fig. 1) shows the Lower Klamath subregion crossing the California-Oregon line,
and the paper does not split it by state. These two subregions are the closest
match to the Klamath Basin but are not the same boundary as the basin's HUCs.

**Species:** Ducks (dabbling and diving, by species), geese, Tundra Swan and
American Coot, including Cinnamon Teal.

**Findings:** Cinnamon Teal use-days are spread across the region, with 39% in
the two Klamath subregions, compared with 80% for all waterfowl. Details below.

## Where the data come from

All counts are from aerial surveys flown for this study (pages 411-412 of the
paper). The paper summarizes them; the survey-level counts are not in it.

-   **Surveyors.** U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and Oregon Department of Fish
    and Game biologists: Jim Hainline (Lower Klamath and Northeast California
    subregions, the southern part of Upper Klamath and Modoc Plateau, and
    Madeline Plains), and Elizabeth Huggins with Meg Laws or Marty St. Louis
    (Warner Valley, Summer Lake, Malheur, and the northern parts of Upper Klamath
    and Modoc Plateau). The authors credit >10 to >30 years of aerial survey
    experience.
-   **Method.** Two single-engine, high-wing aircraft flew at 30-50 m and
    140-150 km/hr. Where habitat blocks were large (most NWRs), pilots flew
    parallel transects 0.4 km (Hainline) or 0.8 km (Huggins, Laws/St. Louis)
    apart and counted birds within a 0.4-km swath. Small or linear habitats were
    flown in a track along them. Large flocks were circled. Estimated counts
    were dictated while flying and entered into a database.
-   **Dates.** 2002: 3-5 Jan, 21-22 Feb, 13-14 Mar, 27-28 Mar, 18-19 Apr, 2-3 May.
    2003: 5-6 Jan, 20-22 Feb, 12-18 Mar, 1-8 Apr, 14-18 Apr, 30 Apr-4 May. The
    authors standardized these to 5 Jan, 21 Feb, 13 Mar, 30 Mar, 16 Apr and 3 May.
-   **From counts to Table 4.** Use-days were calculated by assuming linear
    change in abundance between survey dates. Average birds per day (bpd) is use-days
    divided by 119, the number of days in 5 January-3 May. Table 4 gives total
    use-days and the percent of them in each subregion.
-   **Not surveyed.** Four subregions (Surprise Valley, Shasta Valley, Pueblo
    Valley, and Honey Lake apart from the Madeline Plains) were not surveyed.
    The surveyed area is 76% of SONEC's land, 90% of its wetlands and 96% of
    the satellite-tagged pintail locations in 2002-2003.
-   **Unpublished sources.** Earlier reports by the same group, Fleskes and
    Battaglia (2002, progress report; 2004, final report, USGS Western Ecological
    Research Center), and unpublished data cited for wetland area.
-   **Funding.** Tuscany Research Institute, a Ducks Unlimited grant to the USGS
    Western Ecological Research Center and the California Waterfowl Association,
    and the USGS Science Support Program.

## Table 4

Transcribed from the paper (p. 422). "<1" and a dash are stored as missing.

```{r fy-table4}
lt1 <- NA_real_ # the paper prints "<1"

subregions <- c(
  "Lower Klamath", "Upper Klamath", "Northeast California",
  "Modoc Plateau", "Summer Lake", "Warner Valley", "Malheur"
)

table4 <- tribble(
  ~species, ~level, ~total_use_days, ~`Lower Klamath`, ~`Upper Klamath`, ~`Northeast California`, ~`Modoc Plateau`, ~`Summer Lake`, ~`Warner Valley`, ~Malheur,
  "Dabbling ducks", "group", 68077400, 66, 12, 5, 7, 6, 4, 1,
  "Northern Pintail", "species", 32068600, 57, 15, 4, 8, 8, 6, 1,
  "Northern Shoveler", "species", 12606200, 84, 4, 4, 2, 3, lt1, 1,
  "American Wigeon", "species", 9586900, 71, 10, 6, 7, 4, 2, lt1,
  "Green-winged Teal", "species", 8355100, 74, 11, 5, 9, lt1, lt1, lt1,
  "Mallard", "species", 3222800, 67, 8, 8, 6, 7, 2, 1,
  "Gadwall", "species", 2141600, 66, 6, 13, 7, 6, 2, lt1,
  "Cinnamon Teal", "species", 96300, 26, 13, 21, 18, 17, 2, 3,
  "Wood Duck", "species", 0, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA,
  "Diving ducks", "group", 14538500, 49, 41, 4, 2, 3, 1, 1,
  "Ruddy Duck", "species", 4633600, 54, 41, 5, lt1, lt1, lt1, lt1,
  "Scaup", "species", 4192700, 40, 49, 5, 2, 3, lt1, lt1,
  "Bufflehead", "species", 2148400, 60, 34, 2, 3, 1, lt1, lt1,
  "Canvasback", "species", 1687200, 58, 24, 5, 3, 8, 2, lt1,
  "Mergansers", "species", 912400, 42, 52, lt1, 1, 1, 3, lt1,
  "Ring-necked Duck", "species", 687100, 36, 44, 10, 3, 7, lt1, lt1,
  "Goldeneyes", "species", 139500, 34, 53, lt1, 2, 3, 1, 7,
  "Redhead", "species", 137700, 46, 26, 8, 9, 5, 6, 1,
  "Geese", "group", 34558100, 72, 5, 7, 6, 4, 1, 5,
  "Snow Goose and Ross's Goose", "species", 17531600, 73, lt1, 5, 8, 5, lt1, 9,
  "White-fronted Goose", "species", 14973200, 79, 7, 9, 4, 1, lt1, lt1,
  "Canada Goose", "species", 2053200, 23, 20, 7, 11, 17, 12, 9,
  "Tundra Swan", "species", 2974170, 48, 22, 5, 11, 4, 9, lt1,
  "American Coot", "species", 7878900, 69, 16, 7, 3, 2, 1, 1,
  "All waterfowl", "group", 128027000, 66, 14, 6, 6, 4, 3, 2
)

# Transcription checks. Species add up to their group and the groups to the
# total (within the paper's rounding to 100), and each row's percentages add up
# to about 100 (each "<1" can hide up to 1 point).
group_of <- c(
  rep("Dabbling ducks", 8), rep("Diving ducks", 8), rep("Geese", 3),
  "Tundra Swan", "American Coot"
)
species_rows <- table4 |>
  filter(level == "species") |>
  mutate(group = group_of)

by_group <- species_rows |>
  summarise(species_sum = sum(total_use_days), .by = group) |>
  left_join(table4 |> select(group = species, reported = total_use_days), by = "group")

top_level_sum <- table4 |>
  filter(species %in% c("Dabbling ducks", "Diving ducks", "Geese", "Tundra Swan", "American Coot")) |>
  pull(total_use_days) |>
  sum()

pct_sum <- table4 |>
  filter(total_use_days > 0) |>
  select(all_of(subregions)) |>
  rowSums(na.rm = TRUE)

stopifnot(
  "species rows do not add up to their group" =
    all(abs(by_group$species_sum - by_group$reported)[by_group$group %in% c("Dabbling ducks", "Diving ducks", "Geese")] <= 200),
  "groups do not add up to All waterfowl" =
    abs(top_level_sum - table4$total_use_days[table4$species == "All waterfowl"]) <= 200,
  "row percentages do not add up to ~100" = all(abs(pct_sum - 100) <= 7)
)

table4 |>
  mutate(across(all_of(subregions), \(x) ifelse(is.na(x), ifelse(total_use_days == 0, "-", "<1"), as.character(x)))) |>
  select(-level) |>
  kable(
    format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
    col.names = c("Species or group", "Total use-days", subregions),
    align = c("l", rep("r", 8))
  )
```

## Cinnamon Teal in the Klamath subregions

Cinnamon Teal is much more evenly spread than most species. The two Klamath
subregions hold about 39% of its use-days, against 80% for all waterfowl.

```{r fy-teal}
dist <- table4 |>
  filter(species %in% c("Cinnamon Teal", "All waterfowl")) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(subregions), names_to = "subregion", values_to = "pct") |>
  mutate(
    subregion = factor(subregion, levels = subregions),
    species = factor(species, levels = c("Cinnamon Teal", "All waterfowl"))
  )

ggplot(dist, aes(subregion, pct, fill = species)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Cinnamon Teal" = "#eb6834", "All waterfowl" = "#2a78d6"), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = \(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(
    title = "Where spring waterfowl use-days fall, by subregion",
    subtitle = "Average of 2002 and 2003 (Fleskes and Yee 2007, Table 4)",
    x = NULL, y = "Share of use-days"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1))
```

Average birds per day (bpd) in the two Klamath subregions, from the use-days
and the 119-day season. The percentages are rounded to whole numbers, so each
subregion is good to about half a point, and a "<1" is counted as 0. These are approximations.

```{r fy-klamath}
klamath <- table4 |>
  filter(total_use_days > 0) |>
  mutate(
    klamath_pct = coalesce(`Lower Klamath`, 0) + coalesce(`Upper Klamath`, 0),
    klamath_use_days = total_use_days * klamath_pct / 100,
    klamath_bpd = klamath_use_days / 119
  )

klamath |>
  transmute(
    `Species or group` = species,
    `Lower Klamath (%)` = ifelse(is.na(`Lower Klamath`), "<1", as.character(`Lower Klamath`)),
    `Upper Klamath (%)` = ifelse(is.na(`Upper Klamath`), "<1", as.character(`Upper Klamath`)),
    `Both (%)` = klamath_pct,
    `Approx. use-days` = round(klamath_use_days, -2),
    `Approx. birds per day` = round(klamath_bpd, ifelse(klamath_bpd < 1000, -1, -2))
  ) |>
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","), align = c("l", rep("r", 5)))

# Guards the static text above.
ct <- klamath |> filter(species == "Cinnamon Teal")
aw <- klamath |> filter(species == "All waterfowl")
stopifnot(
  "Cinnamon Teal Klamath share is not 39%" = ct$klamath_pct == 39,
  "All waterfowl Klamath share is not 80%" = aw$klamath_pct == 80,
  "Cinnamon Teal bpd is not about 300" = round(ct$klamath_bpd, -2) == 300
)
```

For Cinnamon Teal that is about `r format(round(ct$klamath_use_days, -2), big.mark = ",")`
use-days, or roughly `r round(ct$klamath_bpd, -1)` birds per day on average
over the season, out of about 900 for the whole study region (Table 1, p. 413).

## Cautions

-   **Two years.** This is a 2002-2003 snapshot, with the 2002-2003 average used
    for Table 4. It says nothing about trends.
-   **Spring migration, not breeding.** The surveys run 5 January-3 May and
    include migrants passing through. They are not the CDFW May breeding index
    in Report 1, so the two cannot be added or compared directly.
-   **No state split.** Upper Klamath is north of the state line in Fig. 1, but
    Lower Klamath crosses it, so California and Oregon cannot be separated.
-   **Detection.** The authors note that drab waterfowl in small groups in
    vegetated habitat were probably missed more often (p. 426), which is a
    concern for Cinnamon Teal. The counts are pseudo-censuses with no precision
    estimates.
-   **Percentages are rounded**, and "<1" cells are unknown.

## Conclusion for Report 2

**We can say where Cinnamon Teal spent the spring in 2002-2003 across
subregions, and that about 39% of its use-days were in the Lower and Upper
Klamath subregions.** We cannot give California and Oregon separately, a
time series, or counts for the Klamath Basin boundary itself.

# Report 3: Oregon Breeding Waterfowl Population Report, 2026

**Source:** Walton, K., and B. Reishus. 2026. *2026 Oregon Breeding Waterfowl
Population Report*. Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife (ODFW), Migratory
Game Bird Program. PDF (34 pages) in `data-raw/waterfowl/reports/`; add a
link here if the report is posted online.

**Temporal Coverage:** Annual, 1994-2026, except 2001 and 2020. The 2026 survey
was flown April 27-29 in western Oregon and May 8-14 in eastern Oregon.
Statewide estimates by species are given for every year (Appendix C). Estimates
by stratum are given only for 2026, 2025 and the long-term average (LTA, the
mean of 1994-2025).

**Spatial Grain:** Stratum. Oregon has five strata and the report gives each
species' estimate for each, plus a statewide total. Flight transects are mapped
(Fig. 1), but observations by location are not published.

**Klamath coverage:** Partial, and Oregon only. The *Southeast Seasonal Marsh*
stratum includes Upper Klamath, Lower Klamath, Klamath Marsh, the Sprague River
Valley and Sycan Marsh, together with many other basins in Lake, Harney and
Malheur counties (Summer Lake, Warner Valley, Catlow Valley, Harney Basin, and
others). The Klamath cannot be separated from them. The *Forested Wetlands*
stratum runs along the California border north to about Quartz Mountain. The
survey does not cover California.

**Species:** 21 duck, goose, coot and crane species or groups, including Cinnamon
Teal. Species that do not breed in Oregon (for example tundra swan and white
geese) are ignored.

**Findings:** Cinnamon Teal can be reported for the Southeast Seasonal Marsh
stratum, which holds 89% of Oregon's. Nothing finer. Details below.

## Where the data come from

The counts come from ODFW's own helicopter survey, described on pages 2-5 of
the report.

-   **Surveyors.** Two ODFW biologists per flight crew, with a contracted
    helicopter and pilot (a Bell 206 B3 flown by JL Aviation Inc. since 2014).
    The Klamath and Lake counties and southern Harney County were flown by one
    crew (Appendix A).
-   **Method.** Transects run through each stratum and are ¼ mile wide (660 feet
    each side of the centerline), covering about 4-5% of each stratum. The
    helicopter flies at 100-200 feet. Observers record every bird on voice
    recorders, with GPS tablets showing the transect boundaries, and the pilot
    loops back or hovers so the observers can try to count everything. Since 2004
    all surveys have been flown by helicopter, detection is treated as complete,
    and no visibility correction is applied.
-   **Counting rules.** Ducks are classed as pairs, lone drakes, lone hens (for
    four diving species only), grouped drakes and flocks. A lone drake or group
    of 2-4 drakes is doubled to account for an unseen hen ("total indicated
    birds"). Larger groups of drakes are flocks and are not doubled.
-   **To a population index.** Counts per transect are expanded by transect
    length and stratum area to a stratum estimate, and the strata are summed. It
    is an index, not absolute abundance. For eastern Oregon, flocks are
    included, which differs from California, which ignores flocked shovelers
    entirely (p. 7).

## Cinnamon Teal

Transcribed from Appendix B (stratum table, p. 16) and Appendix C (annual
estimates, p. 32).

```{r or-teal-tables}
or_teal_strata <- tribble(

  "Willamette Valley", 619, 697, 1552,

)

or_teal_year <- tribble(
  ~year, ~estimate, ~se,

  1997, 49027, 7278,

  2022, 22059, 3736,

)

# Transcription checks against the report's own totals and averages.
stopifnot(
  "strata do not add up to the statewide 2026 estimate" =
    abs(sum(or_teal_strata$est_2026) - 29738) <= 2,
  "annual series does not match the report's 2026 estimate" =
    or_teal_year$estimate[or_teal_year$year == 2026] == 29738,
  "mean of 1994-2025 does not match the report's LTA of 32,293" =
    abs(mean(or_teal_year$estimate[or_teal_year$year <= 2025]) - 32293) < 1,
  "2001 and 2020 should be absent" = !any(c(2001, 2020) %in% or_teal_year$year)
)

or_teal_strata |>
  mutate(share_2026 = est_2026 / sum(est_2026)) |>
  kable(
    format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
    digits = 2,
    col.names = c("Stratum", "2026", "2025", "LTA (1994-2025)", "Share of 2026 total"),
    align = c("l", rep("r", 4))
  )
```

```{r or-teal-plot}
lta <- mean(or_teal_year$estimate[or_teal_year$year <= 2025])

ggplot(or_teal_year, aes(year, estimate)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = lta, color = "grey50", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_pointrange(
    aes(ymin = estimate - se, ymax = estimate + se),
    color = "#eb6834", size = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_line(color = "#eb6834", linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 1996.5, y = lta - 4000, label = "Long-term average", hjust = 0, size = 3, color = "grey35") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma, limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(
    title = "Cinnamon Teal breeding index, Oregon statewide",
    subtitle = "Bars are plus or minus one standard error; no survey in 2001 or 2020",
    x = NULL, y = "Estimated birds"
  )
```

The Southeast Seasonal Marsh stratum has about 89% of Oregon's Cinnamon Teal
(26,405 of 29,738 in 2026, with a long-term average of 25,965), so the
statewide series mostly reflects it. Series by stratum are not published, only
the three values above.

## Other waterfowl in the Southeast Seasonal Marsh stratum

Estimates for the stratum that contains the Oregon Klamath, for 2026, with the
statewide total for comparison.

```{r or-se-species}
or_se_species <- tribble(
  ~species, ~se_marsh, ~statewide,
  "Mallard", 41079, 75668,
  "Gadwall", 50685, 62948,
  "American Wigeon", 204, 1362,
  "Green-winged Teal", 204, 1191,
  "Blue-winged Teal", 41, 169,
  "Cinnamon Teal", 26405, 29738,
  "Northern Shoveler", 8236, 10131,
  "Northern Pintail", 817, 1162,
  "Wood Duck", 82, 3096,
  "Redhead", 4414, 5639,
  "Canvasback", 1206, 1206,
  "Scaup", 2309, 4031,
  "Ring-necked Duck", 2146, 4727,
  "Goldeneye", 0, 0,
  "Bufflehead", 1635, 2628,
  "Ruddy Duck", 3004, 5015,
  "Common Merganser", 715, 886,
  "Hooded Merganser", 0, 0,
  "Canada Goose", 24504, 45579,
  "American Coot", 64909, 69144,
  "Sandhill Crane", 1104, 1661
)

# Statewide values should match Table 1 (p. 6); the stratum cannot exceed them.
stopifnot(
  "a stratum estimate exceeds its statewide estimate" =
    all(or_se_species$se_marsh <= or_se_species$statewide),
  "Table 1 spot check failed" =
    or_se_species$statewide[or_se_species$species == "Mallard"] == 75668 &&
      or_se_species$statewide[or_se_species$species == "Canada Goose"] == 45579,
  "Cinnamon Teal rows disagree" =
    or_se_species$se_marsh[or_se_species$species == "Cinnamon Teal"] == or_teal_strata$est_2026[1],
  "Summary text says 19 of 21 species were present" =
    sum(or_se_species$se_marsh > 0) == 19 && nrow(or_se_species) == 21
)

or_se_species |>
  mutate(share = se_marsh / statewide) |>
  kable(
    format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
    digits = 2,
    col.names = c("Species", "Southeast Seasonal Marsh", "Oregon total", "Share of Oregon total"),
    align = c("l", "r", "r", "r")
  )
```

Nineteen of the 21 species were present in the stratum in 2026; goldeneye and
hooded merganser were not recorded anywhere in the state.

## Cautions

-   **Stratum, not Klamath.** The stratum is far larger than the Klamath Basin and
    mixes in other basins (Harney, Malheur, Lake). The report's flight crew
    assignments (Appendix A) group Klamath and Lake counties together as well.
-   **An index, not abundance.** Transects cover 4-5% of each stratum and the
    estimates are described as an index of breeding waterfowl.
-   **Cinnamon Teal are probably undercounted.** The report says crews believe
    they are detected less often than other species because of dark coloring and
    their use of flooded emergent vegetation (p. 7).
-   **Large flocks swing the stratum estimates**, mainly shoveler and gadwall in
    the Southeast Seasonal Marsh. The report notes it is not known whether
    these birds are breeders or late migrants.
-   **Habitat in 2026.** Snowpack was record or near-record low in the Klamath
    basin, though wetland conditions in Klamath, Lake and Harney counties were
    fair (p. 6).
-   **Comparing to Report 1.** Both are May breeding surveys, but the two states
    use different methods (Oregon: helicopter with no visibility correction;
    California: mostly fixed-wing plane, with visibility correction factors, and
    no flocked shovelers). Their numbers should not be added.

## Conclusion for Report 3

**We cannot pull Cinnamon Teal or other waterfowl data specific to the Oregon
Klamath from this report.** Counts are by stratum, and the stratum that holds
the Klamath is much larger than the basin. What we can provide is the annual
statewide Cinnamon Teal index from 1994 to 2026, its 2026 value by stratum, and
the 2026 estimates for all species in the Southeast Seasonal Marsh stratum.

**Next step:** ask ODFW's Migratory Game Bird Program (the report's authors)
for transect-level counts or observation locations for the Klamath and Lake
county transects (Appendix A: flown by one crew), which could be summarized for
the Klamath Basin.
